company_name: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited

equity_bridge.item: Corporate Funds investment pool (cash + FVTPL + FVOCI + amortised-cost securities) -- matching asset for stripped Corporate Funds investment income
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 Annual Report note 25, 31 Dec 2025 balance; HK$20,676m cash + HK$1,872m FVTPL + HK$11,115m FVOCI + HK$5,730m amortised cost

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: core_business_revenue_5yr_cagr (Core business revenue, ex-Corporate Funds income and ex-donations; the standard equity-CAGR anchor is not used here)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3.5%/5.4%) diverges >30% from revenue (10.0%/13.8%) and EPS (9.1%/20.9%) CAGRs. This is a structural feature of a ~90% dividend-payout policy, not a data-quality issue: HKEX retains only ~10% of earnings, so book value compounds far slower than the underlying earnings power. Revenue/EPS CAGR is used as the growth anchor instead of the (understated-by-policy) equity CAGR. Note FY2025 (+32% core revenue YoY) was a cyclical peak following the 2022-2023 trough (-9% then +3%) -- the 3yr window is inflated by that low base and the 5yr figure (10.0%) is used as the more representative anchor for the historical read, with the forward path independently decelerated (see assumptions.base).

scenario_narratives.base: Cyclical moderation off FY2025/H1-FY2026 record volumes into a structurally growing but more normal mid-single-digit trajectory, carried by Stock Connect deepening and the IPO reform pipeline; capex normalizes once the HQ acquisition completes in FY2027.
scenario_narratives.bull: The capital-diversification-into-Asia thesis compounds without a sentiment interruption: Stock Connect, IPO pipeline and LME all keep setting records, and operating leverage lifts margins above the FY2025 peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: A China/HK sentiment or political shock (echoing 2022-2023), compounded by an adverse LME nickel-litigation outcome and falling-rate pressure on Margin Funds income, cuts volumes sharply in year 1 with only a modest, structurally-capped recovery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: HKEX is valued as an asset-light, high-margin, regulatory-monopoly operating company on owner FCF -- not as a bank, REIT or LIC. Participant margin and clearing-fund balances are excluded entirely (fully matched asset/liability pairs generating no net exposure beyond the investment spread already inside core business revenue); only the Group's own Corporate Funds treasury income is stripped as non-operating and offset by its matching asset in the bridge. The valuation deliberately does NOT extrapolate the FY2025/H1-FY2026 cyclical-peak growth rate, and caps the terminal multiple at 18x to avoid capitalizing today's rich ~22-23x EV/core-EBITDA market multiple into perpetuity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Trading-volume cyclicality: core business revenue is directly tied to ADT/ADV and IPO fundraising, both of which have historically swung double digits year to year (2021 peak -> 2022 -9% -> 2025 record +32%)
HK/Mainland political and regulatory risk: franchise value is inseparable from confidence in Hong Kong's rule of law and its special capital-account access to Mainland China
LME litigation overhang: the September 2026 Elliott Competition Appeal Tribunal claim over the 2022 nickel crisis is unresolved and could result in fines, damages or further reputational damage
Interest-rate sensitivity of Margin Funds investment income (inside core revenue) and Corporate Funds income (stripped, valued via its matching asset) -- both compress in a falling-rate environment
Capex-supercycle execution: the HK$6.3bn HQ acquisition and the 2028 Orion Derivatives Platform build are large, multi-year commitments with limited near-term revenue offset
Terminal-value dependency at an 8.5% WACC / 3.5% terminal growth on a business whose historical growth has been lumpy rather than smooth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 360.0-460.2 HKD

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual Report FY2025 Key Financials table; Employee share-based compensation reserve movement (note 43); no separate cash-tax-on-equity-awards line disclosed, HKEX settles awards via Share Award Scheme share purchases (ShareRepurchases KPI) not net-share withholding, so cash-flow add-back is treated as the full economic cost
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (diluted weighted-average EPS note; 1,267,836,895 shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026)
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD filer and HKD quote (no FX conversion needed). HKD tracks USD closely under the Linked Exchange Rate System, so a USD-adjacent risk-free rate applies. 8.5% base WACC reflects a regulatory-monopoly, high-margin exchange operator (lower systematic risk than a generic industrial) netted against real trading-volume cyclicality and HK/China political-risk exposure that a pure utility WACC would understate. Held constant across scenarios per the 'charge risk once' rule -- cyclicality is carried in the growth/margin paths, not stacked again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial: lease liabilities HK$851m (FY2025) / HK$796m (H1 FY2026) and lease interest ~HK$41m/yr against a >HK$20bn core-EBITDA base (under 0.2%). Left inside reported EBITDA/D&A as disclosed (treatment B in substance -- IFRS 16 ROU depreciation is already inside the reported D&A used for the cash-tax EBIT build) with lease liabilities excluded from the net-debt bridge; the amount is too small to move the valuation either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is trivial (HK$582m equity, ~HK$83-86m annual profit share, <0.5% of NOPAT) and is left inside consolidated flows on an attributable basis -- 'Profit attributable to shareholders' is the NOPAT anchor throughout, so NCI's income share is already excluded. No separate NCI deduction added to the bridge.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing table, 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). HKEX is NOT a bank in the routing-table sense: participant margin/clearing-fund deposits (HK$269bn + HK$34bn at FY2025) sit on the balance sheet as a fully-matched asset/liability pair (derivative financial instruments and margin cash both gross up symmetrically) and generate NO net revenue exposure to HKEX beyond the investment spread the Group earns managing them -- that spread is already inside 'Core business revenue' via segment allocation (see 'Net Investment Income of Margin Funds and Clearing House Funds' note, HK$3,241m FY2025, allocated to Cash/Derivatives/Commodities/FIC segments). Modelling participant margin as deposit funding (bank route) or discounting AFFO post-financing (REIT route) would both be wrong; this is a fee-plus-spread operating business with real capex and real owner FCF.

REVENUE BASE = 'Core business revenue' (HK$27,103m FY2025), which EXCLUDES two items reported separately in the Group's own P&L split: (1) HKEX Foundation donation income (HK$188m FY2025), which is matched pound-for-pound by an equal donation expense inside opex and is a pure pass-through with no owner-FCF effect -- immaterial and left out of both revenue and opex for cleanliness; (2) 'Net investment income of Corporate Funds' (HK$1,870m FY2025), HKEX's own treasury book (cash, FVTPL/FVOCI equities, amortised-cost debt securities; HK$39,393m total at 2025-12-31), which is genuinely non-operating investment income on the Group's own capital, NOT a function of trading volumes or the clearing franchise. STRIPPED per the excluded-income/matching-asset rule (adaptations doc 7d) and its source asset (the full HK$39,393m Corporate Funds pool) added to equity_bridge rather than folded into 'cash' -- this avoids double-counting, since the Corporate Funds note's own cash sub-line (HK$20,676m) already contains essentially all of the Group's narrow cash balance (HK$19,353m per the cash-flow statement), so inputs.cash is set to 0 and net_debt = total_debt (borrowings only, HK$398m) to avoid counting that cash twice.

CAPEX SUPERCYCLE: HKEX is mid-acquisition of its permanent HQ premises for a total HK$6.3bn consideration, being paid in phases 2026-2027 (HK$2,433m spent FY2025, HK$2,447m spent H1 FY2026 alone -- pace has if anything accelerated; only HK$1,149m of committed balance remained undrawn at 2026-06-30). last_fcf (HK$13,286m) is built on FY2025 ACTUAL capex (HK$4,296m, including the HK$2,433m HQ tranche) -- deliberately not normalized, so FY0 owner FCF is conservative/realistic. The capex_pct_path tapers from 16% (FY2026, still finishing the HQ buy) to a steady-state ~6.8% of core revenue (FY2028+), in line with the pre-HQ-programme FY2021-2024 'Others' capex range (5.6-7.4% of core revenue) plus ongoing Orion Derivatives Platform (targeted 2028) technology spend.

SBC is small (1.3% of core revenue) and HKEX settles equity awards by purchasing shares for its Share Award Scheme (a cash outflow captured in ShareRepurchases, not net-share tax withholding), so the reserve-movement SBC figure is treated as the full economic cost with no separate equity-award-tax add-on. Share count held FLAT per the standard rule (SBC expensed once; buybacks are the flat-count funding mechanism, and HKEX's Share Award Scheme purchases already fund the flat count seen in the weighted-average share count barely moving 1,247m (FY2018) to 1,267.5m (H1 FY2026) despite 8 years of grants).

HISTORICAL GROWTH: revenue/EPS 3yr and 5yr CAGRs (13.8%/10.0% core revenue; 20.9%/9.1% EPS) diverge sharply from shareholders'-equity CAGR (5.4%/3.5%) -- this is a STRUCTURAL feature of a ~90%-payout compounder, not a data-quality flag: equity compounds slowly because nearly all earnings are distributed as dividends rather than retained. Growth_rate_source is therefore core-revenue CAGR, not equity CAGR, with a divergence note rather than equity-CAGR anchoring.

bear.narrative: A sentiment reversal -- global risk-off, a sharper China growth slowdown, or an erosion of confidence in Hong Kong's rule of law/capital-account openness -- cuts Cash/Derivatives/Stock Connect trading volumes and stalls the IPO pipeline much as 2022-2023 did (core revenue -9% in 2022 after the 2021 peak), compounded by a fresh setback from the September 2026 Elliott LME nickel-litigation claim (adverse ruling, fine, or renewed reputational damage curbing commodities volumes) and by falling HK/US interest rates compressing Margin Funds investment income faster than rebates can be cut. Margins settle near the FY2022-24 trough as largely-fixed staff/IT/compliance costs (including LME litigation defense) do not flex down with lower volumes. Growth recovers only modestly after the year-1 shock, reflecting the structural (not cyclical) nature of the confidence-erosion risk.

base.narrative: FY2026-27 growth moderates from the FY2025/H1-FY2026 cyclical peak (core revenue +32%/+19% YoY) as Cash Market ADT and IPO fundraising normalize off record levels, then settles into a structural high-single-to-mid-single-digit path carried by Stock Connect deepening (Southbound ETF/REIT/insurance-fund access), the 400+ IPO pipeline under eased WVR/Chapter 18C rules, and LME/FIC diversification, decelerating to a 3.5% terminal rate as the business matures. Capex stays elevated through FY2026-27 finishing the HK$6.3bn HQ acquisition, then reverts to a ~6.8%-of-revenue steady state (IT/Orion platform). EBITDA margin holds in the mid-70s, below the FY2025 peak of 77.2% (which benefited from one-off nickel-litigation legal-fee recoveries and non-recurring unlisted-equity valuation gains inside Corporate Funds, already stripped from the revenue base) but above the FY2022-24 trough of 70-72%.

bull.narrative: The global-capital-diversification thesis plays out in full: sustained mainland and international inflows via Stock Connect (accelerated by RMB-counter and insurance-fund access), Hong Kong holds the #1 global IPO ranking through the 400+ pipeline with Chapter 18A/18C tech listings broadening the issuer base, LME volumes keep setting records as the metals hub consolidates share from Singapore/Shanghai rivals, and margin compression from lower interest rates is more than offset by fund-size growth. Operating leverage pushes core-EBITDA margin above the FY2025 peak as revenue scales faster than largely-fixed staff/IT costs.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the 15% house default to 20% because FY2025/H1-FY2026 are cyclical-peak trading volumes that mean-revert on this folder's own read of HKEX's history (2022 core revenue -9% straight after the 2021 peak), because HK/China political and rule-of-law risk is a genuine, hard-to-diversify tail specific to this franchise (not generic macro pessimism), and because the fresh September 2026 Elliott LME competition-tribunal claim is a live, unresolved legal overhang layered on top of volume cyclicality. Bull trimmed from the 35% default to 30% because the bull case needs several independent things to keep going right simultaneously (sustained IPO pipeline, continued Stock Connect expansion, no HK/China shock, no adverse LME ruling) rather than a single lever.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
